missing_evidence.description: Direct pool saturation evidence such as pool waiters, connection acquisition latency, or exhausted connection counts at the incident onset.

contributing_factors: Config change reduced db.pool.max_connections from 50 to 5 shortly before symptoms

p99 latency rose sharply in the same window

missing_evidence.description: Evidence that the new pool setting was intended and safe for expected traffic, or that another config parameter also changed.

contributing_factors: Recent config change is the only observed change near onset

contributing_factors: Timeouts may reflect an application-level handling issue

recommended_actions.text: Restore the database connection pool to a safe value and validate the service under expected traffic; the pool reduction from 50 to 5 is the most plausible trigger for the observed connection-timeout errors, latency spike, and 5xx surge.
If the service is still degraded, temporarily increase available database connections or roll back the pool limit change to relieve request queuing and connection-acquisition timeouts.

Add a deployment/configuration guardrail for db.pool.max_connections changes, including approval, safe defaults, and automated checks that block reductions likely to exhaust the pool under normal load.

Add alerting and dashboards for connection-pool saturation signals, including pool wait time, exhausted connections, and request timeout rates, so future mis-sizing is detected before 5xx errors rise.

Verify whether any upstream dependency of reviews-0ee was slow or failing at incident onset by checking dependency-specific logs and metrics for checkout-23b, media-bbe, session-cache-8e3, and geo-api-38e.
Review application traces and stack details for the connection-timeout path to rule out an underlying code defect that could have been exposed by the pool-size change.
